signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags USD as the weekly leader with an average gain of +2.066% across 9 pairs against NOK as the trailing currency at -1.937% across 2 pairs, establishing a 4.003% spread. Spot trades at 9.565, holding above its SMA20 at 9.368, SMA50 at 9.422, and SMA200 at 9.486. The bilateral divergence is reinforced by short-dated yield momentum, where the Norway 2Y spread versus the US has narrowed by 16bp over 5 sessions to -17bp. Retail sentiment sits at 91% long, exhibiting extreme long positioning against an advancing pair. US 5Y yield decomposition shows a 5-day nominal move of +26bp consisting of real yields rising +25bp and breakevens at +1bp (FRED, as of Nov 12), pointing to a real-yield-led rate advance that sustains broad dollar demand. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, supported by dominant G10 outperformance and widening real-rate drivers. Catalyst: US Retail Sales on 16 Nov — 0.3% m/m expected. Risk: A drop below the SMA200 at 9.486 invalidates the upside momentum.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 159.78, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.22, 157.42, and 158.72, while 160.00 remains the key psychological barrier that has historically prompted official rhetoric. The fundamental backdrop is supported by a Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% policy stance yielding a +267bp SOFR vs TONA carry advantage for USD. However, 1M 25d risk reversals stand at -1.79 (Saxo Bank, indicative mid), showing elevated demand for JPY call protection. Concurrently, USD/JPY ATM implied volatility of 7.3% sits 2.0 percentage points above HV30 at 5.3%, demonstrating a notable vol risk premium. While the carry differential favors USD upside, the persistent options put skew signals active institutional hedging against an abrupt topside rejection near 160.00. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while spot holds above 158.72. Catalyst: Japan preliminary Q3 GDP release. Risk: A break above 160.00 prompting official yen-buying operations.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1029, tracking below its SMA20 at 1.1174, SMA50 at 1.1297, and SMA200 at 1.1527. CFTC data shows institutional Leveraged Funds net short -104,030 contracts, falling into the 2nd percentile of the 52-week distribution with a z-score of -1.80, indicating a crowded institutional short. In sharp contrast, retail positioning is 87% long, setting up an extreme institutional-versus-retail divergence. The rate backdrop maintains a structural USD carry advantage, with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% delivering a +146bp SOFR vs ESTR premium. While Bundesbank President Nagel stated that an ECB hike remains probable, the crowded speculative short profile leaves EUR/USD susceptible to a short squeeze if hawkish rhetoric gains traction across the Governing Council. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD, constrained between institutional short saturation and retail dip-buying. Catalyst: Germany ZEW Economic Sentiment Indicator on 16 Nov. Risk: A daily close below 1.1000 extending institutional trend momentum.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Retail Sentiment vs Carry Trend
signals.text: USD/CAD prints at 1.4269, maintaining an uptrend above its SMA20 at 1.4070, SMA50 at 1.4081, and SMA200 at 1.3910. The macro yield environment reinforces the pair, with Fed at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.50% providing a +137bp SOFR vs CORRA carry advantage in favor of USD. Leveraged funds are net short CAD at -85,289 contracts (25th percentile, z -0.97), whereas retail positioning reflects an extreme 92% short stance, betting heavily on a mean reversion lower. Furthermore, Canadian economic data displays signs of softening, illustrated by an unemployment rate print of 6.7% versus 6.3% expected, registering a +3.00σ shock on the labor surprise index. The confluence of policy divergence, soft domestic indicators, and aggressive retail fading suggests upside trend continuation toward 1.4350. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, aligned with carry advantage and contrarian retail skew. Catalyst: Canada CPI release on 16 Nov — 0.0% m/m expected. Risk: A daily close below the SMA20 at 1.4070 invalidating the immediate trend.
